items.title: RJ Mitte Dies: ‘Breaking Bad’ Actor Was 34
items.summary:
RJ Mitte, the actor who played Walter White Jr. on AMC's "Breaking Bad," has died at 34. Representatives for Mitte confirmed the death Monday, saying he died in Brownsville, Texas, and did not give a cause.

"It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte," his reps said in the statement reported by Deadline. They asked for privacy for the family, and no information about survivors or a memorial service was immediately available.

Mitte, who was born in Jackson, Mississippi on August 21, 1992, had cerebral palsy, as did the character he played opposite Bryan Cranston. "Breaking Bad" ran from 2008 to 2013 and collected 58 Primetime Emmy nominations, winning 16 of them, including two for Outstanding Drama Series. Mitte shared the SAG Award for Ensemble in a Drama Series with the cast in 2014, after nominations in the two previous years.

He used the show's reach to build a second career in disability advocacy, serving as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children's and as president of The Mitte Foundation. He also voiced a role in "HCBS Final Rule: The Animated Series," a set of shorts explaining changes to Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services community-based programs for people with intellectual disabilities in California.

On screen, Mitte starred in the 2021 wrestling drama "Triumph" as a high school senior with cerebral palsy, appeared opposite Dove Cameron in 2024's "Love Me Dead" and opposite Finn Wittrock in this year's "Westhampton." His television credits included "Switched at Birth," "Now Apocalypse" and "The Guardians of Justice (Will Save You!)."

His most recent credit, per IMDb, is the independent drama "Talking to Strangers," in which he starred opposite Lin Yin. The film held a red-carpet screening on September 30 at the Fine Arts Theatre in Beverly Hills, less than two weeks before his death.

items.title: Fontaines D.C. Release New Duet with Rosalía “Where Is Gone?”: Stream
items.summary:
Fontaines D.C. have released "Where Is Gone?," a duet with Rosalía and the third and final single ahead of their fifth album, "Dopamine Chamber." It is the first song in the Irish band's catalog to feature a guest vocalist.

The track is a slow ballad built on weeping strings, with Rosalía and frontman Grian Chatten trading verses before converging on the chorus — his voice pitched low beneath her smoky upper line. The lyrics track a relationship coming apart, with the pair singing "There's no harm in saying leave and let it die" at the refrain's peak.

Guitarist Carlos O'Connell explained the collaboration in a statement cited by Consequence. "I've been a fan of Rosalía since her debut album, which was absolutely beautiful," he said. "What really excited me was how she was keeping a Spanish tradition of music alive, which in a spiritual way felt akin to what we've tried to do with Irish music. For someone with roots in both countries, it's been beautiful to see. She's an artist who's blown me away at every stage since."

"Dopamine Chamber" arrives Friday, October 16. The band previewed it with lead single "Marianne" and follow-up "Tongue." Rosalía, for her part, performed "Reliquia" and "Magnolias" from her 2025 album "LUX" on "Saturday Night Live" last weekend.

Fontaines D.C. begin a European arena run this month with dates in Lisbon, Madrid, Barcelona and Bologna before reaching London's O2 on November 27. Japanese and Australian dates follow in early 2027, including Laneway Festival appearances in Sydney, Brisbane, Melbourne and Auckland.

The band's North American touring splits across two stretches in 2027. A spring leg opens April 23 at MGM Music Hall at Fenway in Boston and runs through San Francisco's Bill Graham Civic Auditorium on May 12, while a fall leg starts September 24 in Columbus and closes October 15 at the Kia Forum in Inglewood.

items.title: MLB Playoffs 2026: Where to Watch Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Milwaukee Brewers Series Live Online
items.summary:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers meet in the 2026 National League Championship Series, a best-of-seven set that decides which club represents the National League in the World Series. Milwaukee holds home-field advantage on the strength of a 103-59 regular season record, the better mark of the two.

The winner advances to face the survivor of the American League Championship Series, where the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays are playing for the pennant. FOX carries the NLCS on broadcast television.

For viewers without cable, The Hollywood Reporter laid out the streaming options that carry FOX. DirecTV offers a five-day trial and then charges $59.99 for the first month of its entry-level Entertainment package, which includes more than 90 channels, before rising to $89.99 per month. Fubo's Pro plan, with more than 230 channels and over 1,000 hours of cloud DVR, runs $63.99 for the first month and $88.99 after, and also comes with a five-day trial for new subscribers.

Sling's Blue plan is the cheaper route at $54.99 per month for more than 40 channels, though channel lineups vary by local market. Hulu + Live TV starts at $49.99 for the first month and $89.99 thereafter, bundling Disney+, ESPN Unlimited, unlimited cloud DVR and more than 100 live channels.

Every NLCS game also streams on FOX One, which carries a three-day free trial and costs $19.99 per month through Prime Video. Amazon offers a 30-day Prime trial for anyone who isn't already a member.

Both ballparks tend to draw recognizable faces. Jason Bateman, Rob Lowe and Billie Eilish have turned up for the Dodgers, while Stephen Colbert and Austin Aries have been spotted supporting Milwaukee.
